protocol.hypothesis: Instruction-conditioned visual-effect similarity predicts subtask outcome better than additive instruction/effect functions.
protocol.features: Existing frozen, pooled before/after/subtask CLIP only; no task group, failure metadata, IDs or labels enter kernels.

blocks.delta: unit(after) minus unit(before), retaining zero and magnitude

protocol.bandwidth: gamma = reciprocal median strictly positive squared pairwise distance among this fit's training rows; gamma=1 for a constant block
protocol.normalization: Each block RBF and each combined kernel has unit diagonal; no dataset-wide learned normalization.
protocol.selection: Inner leave-one-group-out class-balanced group recall; ties choose smaller C; methods are all reported, never selected against outer scores.
protocol.selection_metric: For each class, mean recall over validation groups containing that class; then mean over the two classes. Missing/failed predictions count wrong. This is not ordinary pooled balanced accuracy.
protocol.split: Outer and inner leave-one-group-out; purge training rows sharing any image SHA or episode with validation/test rows at each level.
protocol.failures: Empty training or solver failure yields abstentions without dropping validation/test rows; one-class training uses its sole class.
limits: Only two pooled states and subtask text, no trajectory, action vector, object localization or overall-task reference resolution.
Product kernels change the function class; an improvement is not proof of temporal reasoning or causality.
Nested selection guards C selection only. Method design followed already-seen dataset results and remains exploratory.
Identical observations can receive different outputs for different embeddings, but CLIP may not encode the relevant instruction distinction.
Counterfactual pair labels are never used to select hyperparameters or construct a training feature.
